title: Chromatic Number by treewidth
variant: Undirected graph coloring with an input color budget
task: Can the vertices of G be colored with at most ℓ colors so that adjacent vertices have different colors?
encoding: A finite simple undirected graph G and a positive integer ℓ.

bounds.statement: Under ETH, no deterministic algorithm decides Chromatic Number within the stated running time.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.1 and its cover-size bound, pp. 698–699, with treewidth bounded by vertex cover number
Theorem 6.3, the treewidth bound for Chromatic Number

bounds.statement: Under SH, no deterministic algorithm decides Chromatic Number within the stated running time.

sources.locator: Table 1, Chromatic Number row and footnote d, p. 4, and Theorem 3.1, p. 8

bounds.statement: Under FPT ≠ W[1], no deterministic algorithm decides Chromatic Number within the stated running time.
qualifications: The exponent h(t) is finite and nonnegative. There is a computable function T such that, for every positive integer j, h(t)≤t log₂(t)/j whenever t≥T(j).

reader.label: Effective little-o bound in the treewidth

sources.locator: Theorem 9 and the construction of Lemma 4, especially Claim 12. The lemma fixes the number of colors. For source length S, taking q of order √(log S) keeps the construction polynomial. Encoding choices in base q and adding a q-clique to enforce the lists gives t log(t+2) at most a computable parameter factor times log S.
sources.role: source construction for the unrestricted bound

recoveryAssessments.comparison: The exclusion reaches the historical exponent scale t log₂ t for exponents with effective convergence.

recoveryAssessments.comparison: SH excludes every fixed exponent power below one in the treewidth t. This recovers degree one. The historical little-o family at t log₂ t remains unrecovered.
